messages:
maria (support): FYI customer ACME reporting daily usage CSVs are 'shifted' by one day compared to the Console chart for their org timezone (Asia/Kathmandu / UTC+5:45). They say exports labelled 2026-03-11 contain tokens for 2026-03-12. Can we triage?

jake (analytics): Thanks — can you paste a sample CSV row + the org timezone setting and whether the scheduled export is 'midnight UTC' or 'org local midnight'?

maria (support): Sure. Org timezone: Asia/Kathmandu (UTC+5:45). Export schedule: customer picked "Daily at 00:00" in the UI — it looked like local midnight in the settings but the export filename is 2026-03-11 and the rows include:

```
org_id,day,usage_tokens,timestamp
acme,2026-03-11,1250,2026-03-12T01:15:23Z
acme,2026-03-11,420,2026-03-12T03:02:10Z
```

Console chart (per-day tiles) shows those counts on 2026-03-12. Customer says this started after we rolled the export worker change last week.

jake (analytics): Looks like we labelled the CSV by export job local date but the per-row aggregation uses UTC-to-day mapping. Can you confirm export-bot metadata?

export-bot: scheduled_export_exec {"job_id":"exp-947", "org_tz":"Asia/Kathmandu", "export_time":"2026-03-12T00:00:00+05:45", "server_time":"2026-03-11T18:15:00Z", "cutoff":"UTC_midnight"} :wrench:

sophie (eng-metrics): I pulled the job log. The exporter service is still using the old cutoff policy: day_cutoff is computed as UTC midnight for CSV row assignment. The filename uses org-local date because UI passes tz when naming files, but the backend aggregation call used daily_bucket(ts, 'UTC'). That mismap will shift rows to previous day for positive offsets.

maria (support): Ah — that explains IST/UTC+ zones seeing previous-day rows. Customer wants a fix and backfill for last 7 days if possible. Any quick mitigation?

jake (analytics): Short-term: we can re-run the export with param --use-org-tz=true which will bucket rows by the org's timezone. I'll prepare a one-off job. Need approval to run: may reprocess ~12k rows for ACME.

sophie (eng-metrics): Long-term: change exporter aggregation to call daily_bucket(ts, org_tz) and make the filename consistent with the same bucket. Small patch, but needs to touch metrics pipeline and unit tests. Risk: change affects all orgs that have daily exports; we'll add an explicit feature-flag "exports-org-day-bucket" default on. I can ship a patch to staging today and promote after smoke tests.

maria (support): Customer escalation: they want ETA and whether billing will be impacted. Please give rough times.

jake (analytics): ETA for one-off re-run: 3-4 hours to queue + verify, reprocess 7 days. Backfill script will generate CSVs and we can put them into the same storage location with suffix _corrected. I'll notify billing team about potential duplicate rows; we can mark those as non-billable if exported previously.

sophie (eng-metrics): ETA for prod fix behind a feature-flag: stage deploy this afternoon (~5 hrs inc tests), 24h monitoring, prod roll in 48h if no regressions. Backfill tool: I can extend the reproc to annotate rows with original_job_id so we can reconcile.

maria (support): I'll tell ACME: immediate one-off re-export within 4 hours, and a staged fix in 2 days. Also offering a manual refund/credit if billing double-counts.

jake (analytics): Quick repro steps for engineers:
1) Set org.tz=Asia/Kathmandu
2) Create usage events at UTC times that map to next local day, e.g. 2026-03-12T00:30:00+05:45 -> 2026-03-11T18:45:00Z
3) Trigger scheduled export (server in UTC) and observe filename vs row day assignment

sophie (eng-metrics): I'll open PR with unit tests that assert filename_date == daily_bucket(first_event_ts, org_tz). Assigning to @sophie. Marking feature-flag and adding migration for one-off backfill.

maria (support): Thanks — tagging this P1 for ACME. I'll share updates with customer and confirm whether they want corrected files uploaded to the same S3 path or a new folder.

sophie (eng-metrics): Noted. Also check edge-case: half-hour offsets (UTC+5:30) and 45-minute offsets (Nepal) — our timezone lib needs to honor non-hour offsets. I found a related test failing in tz database mapping; fixing that too.

maria (support): Great, please ping when re-export completes so I can close the escalation. :thumbsup:
